If `i` has a reflector `L`, then the function `(i.obj (L.obj A) ⟶ B) → (A ⟶ B)` given by
precomposing with `η.app A` is a bijection provided `B` is in the essential image of `i`.
That is, the function `fun (f : i.obj (L.obj A) ⟶ B) ↦ η.app A ≫ f` is bijective,
as long as `B` is in the essential image of `i`.
This definition gives an equivalence: the key property that the inverse can be described
nicely is shown in `unitCompPartialBijective_symm_apply`.

This establishes there is a natural bijection `(A ⟶ B) ≃ (i.obj (L.obj A) ⟶ B)`. In other words,
from the point of view of objects in `D`, `A` and `i.obj (L.obj A)` look the same: specifically
that `η.app A` is an isomorphism.

We define this as `monoidal_closed` with respect to the cartesian monoidal structure.

***
*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Closed.Cartesian*

```lean
CategoryTheory.reflector.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (i : D ⥤ C) [Reflective i] : C ⥤ D
```
***
The reflector `C ⥤ D` when `R : D ⥤ C` is reflective. 
***
*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Reflective*

```lean
CategoryTheory.preservesBinaryProductsOfExponentialIdeal.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [Category.{v₁, u₂} D] (i : D ⥤ C) [HasFiniteProducts C] [Reflective i] [CartesianClosed C] [HasFiniteProducts D]
  [ExponentialIdeal i] : PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) (reflector i)
```
***
If a reflective subcategory is an exponential ideal, then the reflector preserves binary products.
This is the converse of `exponentialIdeal_of_preserves_binary_products`.

```lean

  (i : D ⥤ C) [Reflective i] : C ⥤ D
```
***
The reflector `C ⥤ D` when `R : D ⥤ C` is reflective. 
***
*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Reflective*

```lean
CategoryTheory.leftAdjointPreservesTerminalOfReflective.{v, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (R : D ⥤ C) [Reflective R] :
  PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{v + 1}) (monadicLeftAdjoint R)
```
***
The reflector always preserves terminal objects. Note this in general doesn't apply to any other
limit.

***
*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monad.Limits*

```lean
CategoryTheory.preservesFiniteProductsOfPreservesBinaryAndTerminal.{v, v', u, u'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  {D : Type u'} [Category.{v', u'} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) F]
  [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{1}) F] [HasFiniteProducts C] (J : Type) [Fintype J] :
  PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F
```
***
If `F` preserves the terminal object and binary products then it preserves finite products.
